title: The need for an Acharya in one’s spiritual life
body:
The need for an Acharya in one’s spiritual life

One who desires moksham must seek out an Acharya. When one seeks out an Acharya and surrenders at their feet, any sin will not pose any hindrance to moksham. Without an Acharya, regardless of how many good deeds we may commit in our lifetime, we will not be eligible for moksham.
Here are a few anecdotes that elucidate the role of an Acharya in our lives.

Vishnu Dharmam tells the story of Kshethrabandhu, who retorted to evil ways but was reformed by a sage. The sage was pleased by Kshethrabandhu’s attention span and advised him to chant the name of Govinda, and that one day, the Lord would show him the path of righteousness, reforming him. Kshethrabandhu followed the sage’s advice and gained Paramapadam. 

Padmottara Puranam tells the story of Pundarika, who relentlessly practiced bhakti-yoga but could not get a glimpse of the Lord and hence became dejected. One day, Pundarika encountered Devarishi Narada and explained to him what plight he was facing. Devarishi Narada told Pundarika not to worry and gave him the Ashtaakshara Mantram, instructing him to chant and meditate upon it. Pundarika earnestly followed Devarishi Narada’s advice and attained Paramapadam.
